hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: We seek triplets (i, j, k) with i < j < k where (nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k]) % d == 0.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Rearrange the modulo condition: nums[i] % d == (-nums[j] - nums[k]) % d.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Fix j in an outer loop. Before inner loop k > j, maintain frequency map of nums[i] % d for all i < j.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def divisibleTripletCount(self, nums: list[int], d: int) -> int:
        from collections import defaultdict
        count = defaultdict(int)
        ans = 0
        n = len(nums)
        for j in range(n):
            for k in range(j + 1, n):
                rem = (d - (nums[j] + nums[k]) % d) % d
                ans += count[rem]
            count[nums[j] % d] += 1
        return ans
```

variables: n: size of input array or string
